_schema: world size (as a string) -> the measured peak for that world. A key exists only if a run at THAT world size reported it; extrapolating from another world is what gate_memory_measured refuses.
_caveat: Every peak here is RANK 0 (train.py's log line is is_main), so each is a LOWER bound on the worst rank -- per-rank DDP buckets differ. Safe to rule from at 25 GiB of headroom; NOT safe below about 10 GiB, where every rank has to report before the number means anything.
_why_not_nvidia_smi: nvidia-smi reads the caching allocator's reservation, not the high-water mark of live tensors. It returned 74.10 GiB at world=3 and 74.09 at world=7 -- the DDP bucket growth these measurements exist to find is invisible to it, because a larger bucket is served from cache the allocator never returns. Every fits/does-not-fit call in this repo before train.py:2604 (661e5ce) came from that number.

8.config: b32 accum1 d1024 L32 h8 ffn3072 seq4096 grad_ckpt compiled fp8 attn_res-Full
8.note: A BY-PRODUCT of the crash-recovery gate test, not a measurement run: that test trains 60 steps and is killed at 40, so this reading comes from a job that was deliberately terminated. The kill is unrelated to the peak -- it happened after step 40 reported, and the figure had already been flat across four windows by then, one more than the world=7 entry. Recorded because the shape is the launch recipe exactly (mix_500m, all nine domains, same batch/accum/depth/precision) and re-running a dedicated 30-step probe would measure the same thing twice. Identical to world=7's 69.63: per-card activations do not move when a rank is added, which is what DDP predicts and what this now shows rather than assumes.

7_alt_b16a2.config: b16 accum2 -- same 917,504 tok/step as b32 accum1, half the activation set
7_alt_b16a2.role: control, not fallback. Its purpose was to prove the peak field tracks configuration at all -- the prediction that it must read materially lower was recorded in eff.w7_peak_memory_b32_fits before this arm ran. It is also the reserve: where 33 GiB comes from if seq or mix complexity grows.

_model.predicted_from: 493.6M params x 2 bytes x 3 copies (weights + Muon momentum + grads); agreement to 0.19 GiB is what makes this a model rather than a two-point fit
_model.note: Peak is LINEAR in batch. A first reading that grad_ckpt made activations sub-linear was wrong. Extrapolations from this line assume activation memory scales with seq the way it scales with batch, which is UNTESTED -- attention's quadratic term and the KDA recurrent state need not move together. On that assumption seq 8192 puts b32 at ~136 GiB (does not fit) and b16a2 at ~70 GiB (fits), making b32 the ceiling for this card at seq 4096.

4.config: b16 accum2 d1024 L12 h8 ffn3072 seq4096 NO grad_ckpt uncompiled fp8=False attn_res-Full/0 doc_mask
4.source: NOT a new probe. This is the peak the A/B (2a) baseline arm REPORTED while running the data leg's exact configuration: params 206.1M, world 4, and a cfg line that matches the leg flag for flag (batch 16 accum 2 seq 4096 grad_ckpt False lr_scale 1.0 attn_every 4). Running w7_peak.sh again would have spent 30 steps on four cards to re-derive a number already on disk, and w7_peak.sh could not have produced it anyway: it hardcodes --layers 32 and refuses any world but 7.
4.range_over_50_windows: 60.95 - 61.01 GiB, spread 0.06 GiB (8/16/14/8/3/1 windows at 60.95/.96/.97/.98/.99/61.01). The MAX is recorded, not the mean or the modal value -- a fits/does-not-fit call is made against the worst window, and the mean would understate it by 0.05 GiB.
4.mix_difference_is_not_a_memory_differenc: The arm ran data/mix_200m_4b.json and the leg runs data/mix_200m_8b.json. Checked rather than waved past: same 9 domains, and all 9 weight deltas are exactly 0.0 -- the two files differ only in total_tokens (3,999,997,952 vs 8,000,000,000), which sets how many steps run, not what one step allocates. Peak is a per-step high-water mark.
4._caveat_applies: Rank 0 only, like every other row here, so this is a LOWER bound on the worst rank. The file's own rule is that ruling from it needs about 25 GiB of headroom; 34.57 GiB clears that. It clears it by less than the 493.6M/b16a2 arm's 58.93 GiB, because this leg runs WITHOUT grad_ckpt -- 206M unchecked costs more activation memory than 493.6M checkpointed.
